retainedReference.title: Temple of Kom Ombo
retainedReference.reason: Exact mapped identity supplies footprint/centerline and an undirected plan axis. Facade facing, model origin, height datum and visual fit still require review.

geometry.axisMethod: minimum-area rectangle; +X longest axis; direction ambiguous by 180 degrees

pictures.author: Iris Fernandez / AWIB-ISAW
pictures.observations: Actually inspected full frontal photograph: five prominent shafts, varied broad floral capitals, paired entrance axes flanking the central support, low screen walls, broken edges and two surviving upper lintel/cornice bands with winged discs. Night lighting is not baked into materials. The file page camera coordinate is inconsistent with the monument and is not used for placement.

pictures.author: Roland Unger
pictures.license: GFDL and Creative Commons options per file page; viewed only
pictures.observations: Actually inspected oblique daylight view: a compact high stone-beam group on floral columns, low screen walls and roofless broken column stumps across the broad forecourt. Rear wall remains are much lower and irregular. Grey-beige sandstone and people guide scale; no full roof over the court is invented.

pictures.author: Franck Monnier
pictures.license: CC BY-SA3.0 licensing section; viewed only
pictures.observations: Actually inspected capital/entablature close-up rather than an overall view: flared layered floral capital, broad cavetto cornice, large winged disc and worn carved shaft surface. Fine hieroglyphs are not copied or invented as readable text.
